text: Baseline REFUTED (local-full, full precision): on 200 inputs (seed 1) the model's last-position output equals the dataset answer on only 28.5%. Mean logit diff (answer vs foil) 0.075 +/- 0.70 on clean and -0.08 on corrupt, i.e. indistinguishable. Per-example logit diffs are exactly -1, 0 or +1, so the model emits a clean one-hot-like output, it just is not the labelled token. For comparison, in the 64 seed-0 examples (E0001) the answer distribution is roughly 2:42%, 3:38%, 4:14%, 1:6%, 5:2%; matching labels drawn at random from that distribution would give about 0.34, always guessing the mode about 0.42. 28.5% is at or below that. The dataset's answers are not the model's outputs.

text: STOP: no behaviour to explain. Two independent baselines at full precision (E0002: n=200 seed 1; E0003: n=400 seed 2) both give 28.5% agreement between the model's output and the dataset answer, with mean logit diff 0.05-0.08 (std 0.7), the same as on the corrupt inputs. That is the label base rate, not a computed function. The model does emit crisp outputs, but the labels supplied by this dataset do not describe them, so any circuit found by patching against these labels would be an artefact. No screening, patching, predict() or verify_hypothesis was run; 22 of 25 experiments left unused on purpose.
